items.author: Chirag Lala
items.title: The bipartisan permitting bill gets transmission right
items.summary: A brief on the bill's grid title. It says the bill goes further than the 2024 EPRA bill: FERC must permit qualifying interstate lines when a state has not approved them within a year, DOE-identified congested areas replace national interest corridors, and costs follow a beneficiary-pays rule. It also covers the data center cost rule, the right-of-first-refusal ban and advanced transmission technologies, and notes that DOE's transmission loan program needs new money because the One Big Beautiful Bill Act rescinded its funding.

quote.text: Most importantly, BAAJA gives FERC more statutory cover to take aggressive actions on grid development.
quote.speaker: Chirag Lala, Center for Public Enterprise

items.author: Joshua Siegel
items.title: New in @PunchbowlNews: What's next for permitting
items.summary: Siegel posts his Punchbowl News item on what comes next. Utilities may push to weaken the expanded FERC backstop siting authority and the mandatory data center cost language, which the item calls stronger than the voluntary Ratepayer Protection Act that Senate Democrats blocked. Environmental groups are expected to contest the limits on NEPA remedies and the Clean Water Act section 401 changes, and Rep. Jared Huffman said progressives may hold out for more next Congress.

quote.text: Negotiators say they struck a difficult balance that'll be hard to defeat. But landmines are here.
quote.speaker: Joshua Siegel

items.author: Jane Flegal
items.title: The data center language in the permitting deal is the best yet
items.summary: Flegal says the bill makes data centers pay both the full cost of the upgrades they cause and a share of the existing grid. Section 2107 does both for transmission: FERC must charge these loads embedded plus incremental cost, and new Federal Power Act section 228 keeps incremental costs off other customers. Her estimate of billions of dollars a year for ratepayers is her own; the bill gives no figure.

quote.text: forces data centers to pay full costs they cause AND their share of the existing grid.
quote.speaker: Jane Flegal

items.author: Jane Flegal
items.title: The permitting bill is out and it’s awesome
items.summary: A 15-post thread. Flegal credits Whitehouse and Heinrich, calls the permit certainty sections a guard against future administrations, and praises the transmission title's regional and interregional planning, backstop siting and cost allocation rules. She cites C2ES and Greenline Insights modeling of 71 million fewer tons of CO2 in 2035 across the regions studied. Two posts go beyond the text: section 1401 pays delay costs plus 25 to 50 percent of costs incurred, not full reimbursement, and the new EIA reporting falls on utilities, not data centers.

items.author: Todd N. Tucker
items.title: Lots of good in BAAJA, including shrinking our juristocracy & vetocracy
items.summary: Tucker, of the Roosevelt Institute, lists backstop federal siting, NEPA judicial review limits and deadlines, and an end to the administration's actions against wind as gains that return decisions to elected officials. The wind point goes further than the text: the wind and solar side agreement is not in the bill, and section 1402 suits cannot be filed until 180 or 280 days after enactment.

quote.text: it'll re-empower elected officials to do things we elected them to do and save us money and jobs.
quote.speaker: Todd N. Tucker

items.author: Christopher Barnard
items.title: Really positive & good faith statement on permitting reform out of the White House Office of Public Liaison
items.summary: Barnard posts a screenshot of a White House Office of Public Liaison email saying the bill advances the President's agenda. The email lists permit certainty, judicial review changes and transmission permitting among its key provisions. Its claim that issued permits are protected from being overturned is broader than section 1401, which restrains agencies but still lets a court order a revocation.

items.author: Thomas Hochman
items.title: The Permitting Grand Bargain Is Here
items.summary: Hochman walks through each title of the bill and calls it more aggressive than he expected on both grid and conventional permitting reform. He highlights the 150-day NEPA limitations period, the end of injunctions and vacatur for NEPA-only claims, new revocation limits with damages, FERC backstop siting without a designated corridor, and the state referral power over local transmission spending. He expects Senate and House votes in the lame duck. His account of the NEPA remedies, revocation damages and FERC siting matches the text (sections 1110, 1401 and 2101).

quote.text: Third and most importantly, injunctions and vacatur are eliminated outright for NEPA-specific claims.
quote.speaker: Thomas Hochman

items.author: Aidan Mackenzie
items.title: WE HAVE A PERMITTING DEAL
items.summary: Mackenzie, an infrastructure fellow at the Institute for Progress, announces the bill and calls it the best permitting bill the country has gotten. He says both parties got a lot and that it is much bigger than the 2022 Manchin package. The visible opening of the thread describes the bill as 400+ pages, which fits the 417-page text; later posts in the thread were not read.

quote.text: it is easily the best permitting bill we've ever gotten
quote.speaker: Aidan Mackenzie

items.author: Aidan Mackenzie
items.title: So how will the permitting reform deal (BAAJA) get big transmission lines built?
items.summary: Mackenzie, an infrastructure fellow at the Institute for Progress, explains how the bill would fix interregional transmission: neighboring regions must complete joint planning on a common set of benefits, FERC approves cost allocation for the lines they select, and FERC can site qualifying lines when states deny them without a designated corridor. These points match sections 2101 and 2103. His figures on Order 1000 projects and merchant lines are not sourced in the thread and are not checked against the bill.

quote.text: So how will the permitting reform deal (BAAJA) get big transmission lines built?
quote.speaker: Aidan Mackenzie

items.author: Shanu Mathew
items.title: Senate’s permitting deal could make power infrastructure easier to finance while requiring data centers to commit more capital to secure electricity.
items.summary: Mathew, an investor and portfolio manager who writes on energy and infrastructure, lists five terms: the 150-day NEPA challenge window, FERC backstop siting with beneficiary-pays cost allocation, the end of the federal right of first refusal, limits on permit revocation with damages, and data center cost responsibility. His data center description matches the text: loads of 20 MW or more bear incremental generation, storage and grid costs, with financial assurance before construction and recovery continuing if the load exits (section 2107, new FPA section 228).

quote.text: Senate’s permitting deal could make power infrastructure easier to finance while requiring data centers to commit more capital to secure electricity.
quote.speaker: Shanu Mathew

items.author: Zeke Hausfather
items.title: Confused by all the debate about the new permitting reform bill?
items.summary: Hausfather, a climate scientist who writes The Climate Brink, posts a one-page table of the bill's main provisions grouped by whom they help, with his own estimate of each one's effect on emissions. Transmission, renewables and geothermal on public land, historic preservation and offshore wind leasing mostly help clean energy; NEPA deadlines and lawsuit limits, permit certainty and the discrimination damages cut both ways; pipeline, drilling and narrower NEPA scope changes mostly help fossil fuels. The section numbers match the text. His line that courts cannot cancel permits applies to NEPA claims (section 1110), and the emissions sizes are his judgment.

quote.text: Here is a quick cheat-sheet of the most important provisions, and their likely impact on emissions
quote.speaker: Zeke Hausfather

visuals.title: What's in the Senate permitting deal
visuals.text: Ten provisions sorted into mostly helps clean energy, cuts both ways and mostly helps fossil fuels, each with its section numbers and an emissions estimate from small to large.

items.author: Robinson Meyer
items.title: The Senate Permitting Deal Contains a Data Center Double Tap
items.summary: Meyer explains the bill's ratepayer provisions for data centers and crypto miners. FERC would have to price transmission service for these customers at both embedded and incremental cost, a new Federal Power Act section would bar shifting incremental costs to other customers for loads of 20 megawatts or more, and states could set less favorable rates and run open seasons. The piece says the changes would apply to "future data centers" but does not state that section 228 covers only loads that interconnect after enactment and leaves existing arrangements in place.

quote.text: Call it the data center double tap.
quote.speaker: Robinson Meyer

items.title: The Bipartisan Buddies With a Plan to Fix Transmission
items.summary: Reps. Gabe Evans and Scott Peters released the CLEAR Act, which would apply to transmission lawsuits the stricter standards used for gas and hydropower projects. Peters expected a Senate package to include NEPA changes, limits on presidents canceling projects, and Section 401 reform.

quote.text: I think it’s coming together pretty well
quote.speaker: Rep. Scott Peters (D-Calif.)

items.author: Robinson Meyer
items.title: Meta Down, Permitting Odds Up
items.summary: Meyer lays out the six buckets of a likely deal (NEPA and judicial review, transmission, Clean Water Act, permit certainty, historic preservation, everything else) and says Lee's NHPA interest comes from his committee's jurisdiction. Prediction markets jumped to 77 percent that day.

quote.text: A permitting reform deal will probably have six buckets.
quote.speaker: Robinson Meyer, Heatmap

items.author: Robinson Meyer
items.title: What a Permitting Reform Deal Could Look Like (Shift Key, with Daniel Palken)
items.summary: Arnold Ventures' Daniel Palken walks through the history of permitting deals and the six buckets of the current talks, which he calls four-corner negotiations among the EPW and ENR leaders. He says the administration's cancellations and withheld permits are the biggest obstacle to Democratic buy-in.

quote.text: all four parties are really sincerely interested in good faith in getting to a deal
quote.speaker: Daniel Palken, Arnold Ventures

items.author: Robinson Meyer
items.title: Permitting Reform, Data Centers, and More With Senator Heinrich and Secretary Granholm (Shift Key)
items.summary: Recorded in late July. Heinrich said talks were active and that the White House was the biggest wild card, citing new historic preservation regulations, offshore wind stop-work orders and the Pentagon's halt on wind reviews. He also described his connect-and-manage interconnection bill and said he would 'get what you can done' in this Congress.

quote.text: I think the biggest wild card is actually and challenge is the White House because the White House continues to do things that sort of poison the well.
quote.speaker: Sen. Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.)

items.author: Robinson Meyer
items.title: Scoop: A Key Democrat Wants to Break America's Worst Energy Bottleneck
items.summary: Heinrich introduced a bill letting new power plants of any type skip full interconnection studies in exchange for curtailing output when the grid is congested, copying the Texas approach. Heatmap saw it as the kind of technology-neutral bill that could slot into a permitting package.

quote.text: would make it easier for new power plants to hook up to electricity markets across the country
quote.speaker: Heatmap (Robinson Meyer)

items.author: Robinson Meyer
items.title: Freedom (It Won't Slow You Down)
items.summary: Cortez Masto and Cotton released a Senate version of the FREEDOM Act that keeps future presidents from interfering with permitted projects. It dropped the House bill's de-risking compensation program and lets a court appoint a contractor to finish a stalled permit. Heatmap calls such a provision essential to any deal.

quote.text: Most importantly, it jettisons a de-risking compensation program.
quote.speaker: Heatmap (Robinson Meyer)

items.author: Matthew Zeitlin
items.title: The Mystery of the Ratepayer Protection Act
items.summary: Explains why hyperscalers back the bill. Harvard's Ari Peskoe calls the PURPA standard largely symbolic because Congress cannot force state regulators to act, and analysts say data centers are not yet the main driver of past price increases.

quote.text: largely symbolic
quote.speaker: Ari Peskoe, Harvard Law School

items.author: Matthew Zeitlin
items.title: FERC Has a New Plan for Data Centers
items.summary: FERC voted 5-0 to send show cause orders to six grid operators, covering study rules, cost-shift safeguards, co-location, flexible service and proximate generation. FERC chose region-by-region orders over a national rule.

quote.text: If new infrastructure is built to accommodate a data center, and that data center doesn’t show up, residential customers are not left on the hook to pay the costs
quote.speaker: FERC Commissioner David Rosner

items.author: Jael Holzman
items.title: How Has the Rise of AI Changed the Odds of a Permitting Deal? (Q&A with ACORE's Ray Long)
items.summary: ACORE's Ray Long says data center load is a catalyst for permitting reform. He cites 166 gigawatts of needed power over four years, about half for data centers, and says a bill would have to come from a Senate deal in an election year.

quote.text: The data center load is a part of the catalyst to get people talking about it
quote.speaker: Ray Long, ACORE

items.author: E&E News staff
items.title: Permitting deal may come after recess. Negotiators say that's OK.
items.summary: Heinrich said talks would likely run past the August recess and that the White House's attacks on renewables and its proposal to roll back tribal consultation under the historic preservation law made a deal harder. Schatz said a deal could come together in five days once the administration lifts its ban on clean energy. Whitehouse and Heinrich planned to meet Capito and Lee that week.

quote.text: I don’t think it’s too late
quote.speaker: Sen. Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.)

items.author: E&E News staff
items.title: Senators outline future of permitting talks
items.summary: After missing the August target, negotiators set September as the new deadline. Whitehouse wanted to avoid the lame duck and said the administration was 'not even close' on wind and solar. A federal judge in Oregon ordered the Pentagon to complete stalled onshore wind reviews. Environmental groups were wary, especially over how far to limit state Clean Water Act authority.

quote.text: There’s a major reset that they need to get to
quote.speaker: Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.)

items.author: E&E News staff
items.title: Wright meets with Republicans on permitting, but deal remains elusive as ever
items.summary: After a dinner of the four Senate committee leaders and a separate Wright dinner with Republicans, E&E reported broad support for a deal but no clear path. Heinrich said the administration's stalled solar, wind and battery permits were the biggest threat. Whitehouse said Democrats would hold a caucus vote before moving any bill.

quote.text: The thing that is the biggest threat to permitting reform right now is that the Trump administration backslid into a series of stalled-out permits
quote.speaker: Sen. Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.)

items.author: E&E News staff
items.title: Permitting talks live on as DOJ declines to appeal ruling favoring Revolution Wind
items.summary: The administration let the deadline pass without appealing a ruling that blocked the Interior stop-work order on Revolution Wind. Whitehouse had threatened to pause talks again if the administration kept attacking renewables and said an appeal would be inconsistent with progress.

quote.text: We are watching those and would view any appeal as inconsistent with further progress on permitting reform
quote.speaker: Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.)

items.author: E&E News staff
items.title: Whitehouse threatens to blow up permitting talks
items.summary: At an EPW hearing Whitehouse said it made little sense to pursue bipartisan permitting reform while the administration would not faithfully execute the law, citing the Revolution Wind stop-work order and canceled solar approvals. He even threatened to oppose routine water and highway bills.

quote.text: Why would we want to do bipartisan permitting reform during an administration that won’t faithfully execute that law?
quote.speaker: Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.)

items.author: Josh Siegel
items.title: Senate releases NDAA with permitting amendment
items.summary: The Senate Armed Services Committee released its fiscal 2027 defense bill with an amendment by Sen. Angus King to curb the Pentagon's delay in processing wind project permits. Chair Roger Wicker said the dispute needed to be resolved.

quote.text: It needs to be resolved and there’s bipartisan support for that
quote.speaker: Sen. Roger Wicker (R-Miss.)

items.author: E&E News staff
items.title: EPA floats changes to NEPA implementation rules
items.summary: EPA proposed changes to its NEPA procedures to follow the 2023 Fiscal Responsibility Act (two-year, 150-page limits for impact statements), the One Big Beautiful Bill Act fee for faster reviews, and last year's Supreme Court ruling that narrowed the scope of review. CEQ data cited: final impact statements took 2.8 years and 661 pages on average.

quote.text: In recent years, final EISs took an average of 2.8 years to complete while clocking in at an average of 661 pages, according to CEQ reviews.
quote.speaker: E&E News

items.author: E&E News staff
items.title: Data center energy bill hits speed bump
items.summary: Frank Pallone's call for a national data center moratorium overshadowed the Energy and Commerce vote on the Ratepayer Protection Act. The bill would require states to consider a federal cost standard that state regulators could reject. Google, Microsoft and the Data Center Coalition backed it; environmental groups opposed it.

quote.text: we need action, not toothless promises from Big Tech
quote.speaker: Rep. Frank Pallone (D-N.J.)

items.author: Jean Chemnick
items.title: EPA proposal could sideline the public on data center permits
items.summary: A July 1 EPA draft rule would drop federal requirements for public notice and comment when states permit minor pollution sources under Clean Air Act New Source Review. Advocates said it could let states permit data centers and power plants without telling nearby communities.

quote.text: EPA says it will empower states. Environmentalists say it will silence communities.
quote.speaker: E&E News

items.author: E&E News staff
items.title: Heinrich releases data center energy plan
items.summary: Heinrich previewed his GRID Savings Act, which would have FERC require large power users to pay for grid upgrades needed to connect. He said Democrats would make it a priority if he chairs the Energy Committee next year, and he opposed moratoria because they push data centers to places with the weakest rules.

quote.text: Pledges are great, but show me the reality.
quote.speaker: Sen. Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.)

items.author: Emily Yehle
items.title: Special edition: POLITICO's Energy Summit kicks off hot permitting summer (Power Switch)
items.summary: At POLITICO's Energy Summit, Capito and Whitehouse both urged the White House to stop attacking renewables, and White House energy council director Jarrod Agen blamed Democrats for opposing gas pipelines and called New York's water-permit review the kind of rule permitting reform would fix. FERC's Swett said a data center cost action was days away.

quote.text: The governor of New York is using regulation to stop a pipeline — using a water regulation that we’re trying to fix in this permitting reform
quote.speaker: Jarrod Agen, White House National Energy Dominance Council

items.author: Joel Kirkland
items.title: Can Congress get behind this data center bill? (Power Switch)
items.summary: After the 52-0 committee vote on the Ratepayer Protection Act, the newsletter notes the bill echoes a voluntary White House pledge and has a shot in the Senate, though Mike Lee had called data center legislation not a priority. It also reports Sen. David McCormick in line to chair the Energy Committee next Congress.

quote.text: Energy and Natural Resources Chair Mike Lee (R-Utah) has said data center legislation is not currently a “priority”
quote.speaker: POLITICO Power Switch

items.author: Jason Plautz
items.title: Signed, sealed: Can Trump's ratepayer pledge deliver? (Power Switch)
items.summary: Twenty-three Republican governors and more than 200 utilities, co-ops, developers and state officials signed the nonbinding Ratepayer Protection Pledge. A law professor said what 'fair share' means is decided at the state utility regulator level.

quote.text: What ‘fair share’ looks like, when push comes to shove, gets answered at the state utility regulatory level.
quote.speaker: Cale Jaffe, University of Virginia law professor

items.author: Alexander C. Kaufman
items.title: Scoop: New Bipartisan House Bill Would Keep President From Yanking Permits
items.summary: Reps. Harder, Gray, Lawler, Bacon and Edwards introduced the FREEDOM Act, a 77-page bill barring agencies from halting fully permitted projects and creating a compensation fund. Heatmap notes the SPEED Act passed the House with only 11 Democratic votes after an offshore wind carve-out.

quote.text: The FREEDOM Act delivers the smart, pro-growth certainty that critical energy projects desperately need by cutting delays, fast-tracking approvals, and holding federal agencies accountable
quote.speaker: Rep. Josh Harder (D-Calif.)

items.author: Jael Holzman
items.title: Trump Is the Biggest Wild Card in Permitting Reform
items.summary: After the House Natural Resources vote of 25-18, Holzman reports that Democrats in both chambers would not back a deal without limits on the president's power over wind and solar permits. Reps. Levin and Casten proposed a parity rule between fossil and non-fossil projects; Golden's no-rescission language was added in committee.

quote.text: Any deal hinges on the Trump administration providing assurances they’re not going to kill every single clean energy project in existence
quote.speaker: Rep. Mike Levin (D-Calif.)

items.author: Emily Pontecorvo
items.title: The House Just Passed Permitting Reform. Now Comes the Hard Part.
items.summary: The House passed the SPEED Act 221-196 after a late change that exempted agency actions between Jan. 20 and enactment from the bill's anti-revocation language. ACP withdrew its support; Huffman said it was going nowhere in the Senate; Rep. Adam Gray voted yes expecting the Senate to fix it.

quote.text: Even if the House passes this bill today, it is going nowhere in the Senate
quote.speaker: Rep. Jared Huffman (D-Calif.)

items.author: Emily Pontecorvo
items.title: Permitting Reform is Back. What Are We Even Talking About This Time?
items.summary: A guide to the SPEED Act: it would cut the NEPA suit window from up to six years to 150 days, limit suits to people who commented, and set court timelines. Heatmap says Democrats would not agree to a deal that does not bar the president from pulling approved permits.

quote.text: Democrats have said they won’t agree to a deal that doesn’t bar the president from pulling previously-approved permits or otherwise level the playing field for renewable energy.
quote.speaker: Heatmap (Emily Pontecorvo)

items.author: Robinson Meyer
items.title: 'We Proved That America Can Still Build Big Things' (Heinrich on SunZia)
items.summary: In an interview marking SunZia's completion, Heinrich said he was working to get to yes and called transmission an incredibly important piece of a balanced package that could reach 65 or 70 votes.

quote.text: We have to make sure that it’s an effectively balanced package — that’s how you get to 65, 70 votes.
quote.speaker: Sen. Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.)

items.title: Senate permitting bill would expand federal role in transmission siting
items.summary: Reports on BAAJA expanding FERC authority to permit interstate transmission lines, eliminating NIETCs and the federal right of first refusal, with reactions from Rob Gramlich and Devin Hartman.

quote.text: The transmission title as well as the impact of the other sections on transmission development are very well-crafted.
quote.speaker: Rob Gramlich, Grid Strategies

items.title: Senate permitting bill could greatly expand power lines and clean energy
items.summary: Reports that BAAJA transmission directives and advanced grid tech mandates could streamline power line buildouts and unblock clean energy for data centers and load growth.

quote.text: If Congress wanted to expand and de-congest the nation’s transmission grid, these are the policy changes that can get that done
quote.speaker: Rob Gramlich, Grid Strategies

items.outlet: Center for Climate and Energy Solutions
items.title: New Analysis Finds Federal Transmission Reforms Would Slash Power Sector Emissions, Boost Grid Reliability, and Save Consumers Billions
items.summary: C2ES and Greenline Insights model nationwide permitting and transmission reforms, finding $125 billion in cumulative grid savings and $19 billion in lower residential bills through 2040.

quote.text: This analysis shows that practical reforms to transmission planning and interconnection processes can unlock more clean energy, reduce our reliance on natural gas, lower costs for consumers, and help build a cleaner, more reliable electric grid.
quote.speaker: Nat Keohane, C2ES

items.title: Sierra Club Reaction to Permitting Bill Introduction
items.summary: Sierra Club notes the urgency of transmission and clean energy but raises concern over fossil fuel infrastructure acceleration without deployment guarantees.

quote.text: There is no task more urgent than building clean energy and transmission. Congress must act to lower energy bills, protect clean air and water, and transition off of fossil fuels, and that means making it faster and easier to build transmission and clean energy.
quote.speaker: Holly Bender, Sierra Club

items.title: The Permitting Bill: Its Procedural Reforms, Explained
items.summary: Alex Mechanick analyzes BAAJA procedural overhaul, focusing on the end of project-stopping injunctions under NEPA and NHPA in favor of remand to correct errors while projects proceed.

quote.text: The most important reform in BAAJA is that violations of NEPA and NHPA can no longer be the basis for stopping a project. Instead, if a court finds a violation, it remands to the agency to correct the error
quote.speaker: Alex Mechanick

items.author: Emily Pontecorvo
items.title: What a President Can and Can’t Do Under the Senate Permitting Bill
items.summary: Tests the project-certainty sections against past reversals with two former Interior Department lawyers: Keystone XL's presidential permit could still have been revoked, the Spruce mine veto and the Lava Ridge cancellation likely could not, and whether oil and gas leases are covered is left to the courts.

quote.text: This bill is clearly looking backwards at five to 10 years of case studies in how an executive branch can delay or revoke permits, and it is targeted at those case studies
quote.speaker: Travis Annatoyn, former Interior deputy solicitor

items.author: Deborah A. Sivas
items.title: Permitting “Reform” Legislation Would Take a Meat Axe to Environmental Law, When What We Need Is a Surgical Scalpel
items.summary: Argues the 150-day limit changes little and that the direct-harm standing test and the remand-only remedy are the provisions that matter, because a project could be built before its review is fixed.

quote.text: This language, if enacted, effectively guts the core purpose and effect of NEPA.
quote.speaker: Deborah A. Sivas

items.author: Christy Goldfuss
items.title: Hard Questions About the Permitting Bill
items.summary: Calls the transmission provisions good for clean energy but asks for an accounting of how much fossil fuel development the bill would enable, and objects to the limits on EPA's Section 404(c) veto and on state water-quality certification.

quote.text: There is no doubt that these provisions are good for clean energy—really good.
quote.speaker: Christy Goldfuss

items.title: Explaining the Senate Permitting Bill, the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act
items.summary: Section-by-section explainer that sets each provision against current law, from the 14 exclusions from NEPA review to the remand-only remedy, permit certainty and data-center ratepayer rules.

quote.text: Under BAAJA, a NEPA violation alone would no longer stop a project.
quote.speaker: Bipartisan Policy Center

items.title: Broad Environmental Coalition Urges Opposition to Permitting Reform Package
items.summary: Letter from more than 200 groups, among them the Center for Biological Diversity, Food & Water Watch, Friends of the Earth Action and Greenpeace USA, asking Schumer and Jeffries not to advance the bill this year and to wait for the next Congress. NRDC, EDF, the League of Conservation Voters, Earthjustice and the national Sierra Club did not sign.

quote.text: We therefore ask you to refrain from advancing the Senate legislation this year.
quote.speaker: Coalition letter

items.author: Simon August
items.title: Senate Energy Bill Would Fine Any President Who Blocks A Whole Class Of Energy Projects
items.summary: Reports Republican support for the disparate-treatment cause of action, with Sen. Kevin Cramer calling the judicial review changes the most important part of the bill.

quote.text: Section 1402 provides recourse if a future administration tries to use the same playbook
quote.speaker: Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee spokesperson

items.author: Sen. Martin Heinrich
items.title: Heinrich on what the permitting bill does for prices and data centers
items.summary: Sponsor's case for the bill on cost, data-center charges and clean energy jobs.

quote.text: If we want to force data centers to pay their fair share and then some, we need permitting reform.
quote.speaker: Sen. Martin Heinrich

items.author: Jane Flegal
items.title: Flegal: the bill is good for transmission, clean energy and electrification
items.summary: Responds to climate groups opposing the bill.

quote.text: But it's good for transmission, clean energy, & electrification. I don’t see how that isn’t a win for climate.
quote.speaker: Jane Flegal

items.author: Pacific Legal Foundation
items.title: Pacific Legal Foundation urges quick passage
items.summary: Property-rights litigation group backs the bill.

quote.text: PLF urges Congress to pass it quickly.
quote.speaker: Pacific Legal Foundation

items.author: Brandon Tatum
items.title: NGA Statement on Permitting Reform
items.summary: The association's chief executive, Brandon Tatum, says NGA is encouraged by the bill's introduction and will work with Congress to develop it further.

quote.text: The National Governors Association and its partners are encouraged by the introduction of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 and look forward to working with Congress to further develop this legislation.
quote.speaker: Brandon Tatum, NGA chief executive

items.author: State of Montana Newsroom
items.title: Gianforte urges Congress to pass federal permitting reform
items.summary: Montana Gov. Greg Gianforte says he joined 21 other Republican governors in a joint statement urging Congress to pass permitting reform. The statement names the bill and asks that it go to President Trump.

quote.text: Republican governors urge Congress to act swiftly, pass meaningful permitting reform, and send this legislation to President Trump's desk.
quote.speaker: Joint statement of 22 Republican governors

letter.ask: Pass permitting reform and send the legislation to President Trump.

items.author: Bill Owens
items.title: NAHB Applauds Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act
items.summary: NAHB's chairman credits the four sponsors with the most meaningful federal permitting reforms in decades and points to the Clean Water Act nationwide-permit provisions.

quote.text: NAHB applauds Senators Lee, Capito, Heinrich and Whitehouse and for their leadership and bipartisan approach to crafting the most meaningful reforms in decades to several key federal environmental permitting programs.
quote.speaker: Bill Owens, NAHB chairman

items.outlet: Office of Sen. Edward J. Markey
items.author: Sen. Edward J. Markey
items.title: Senator Markey Statement on Bipartisan Permitting Reform Proposal
items.summary: Markey says he is still reviewing the text, warns against locking in more fossil fuels and locking out communities, and takes no position.

quote.text: I’m still reviewing text of this proposal, and I will be looking closely at the details.
quote.speaker: Sen. Edward J. Markey

items.author: Blue Dog Coalition
items.title: Blue Dog Statement on Bipartisan Permitting Reform Agreement
items.summary: The House Blue Dog Coalition backs the Senate bill, notes that it carries parts of the SPEED Act, and asks House and Senate leaders to bring it to a floor vote in November.

quote.text: We urge House and Senate leadership to bring this bill to the floor for a vote in November.
quote.speaker: Blue Dog Coalition

items.author: Matthew Zeitlin
items.title: Miners Struck Gold With the Senate Permitting Bill
items.summary: Heatmap reports that the bill's mining-waste provision would settle a 2022 court problem for hardrock mines such as Rosemont.

quote.text: The proposal resolves an issue that has bedeviled the industry since 2022.
quote.speaker: Matthew Zeitlin, Heatmap

items.author: Ryan M. Bernstein, Bernard L. McNamee
items.title: Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 Proposes Sweeping Reform for Energy and Infrastructure Projects
items.summary: Law-firm alert on the September 30 agreement. It covers the permitting and environmental review changes plus the transmission and large-load provisions, and notes the bill still needs both chambers.

quote.text: Senate committee leaders reached a bipartisan agreement on Sept. 30, 2026, on sweeping permitting reform for energy and infrastructure projects, but the bill still needs Senate and House approval
quote.speaker: McGuireWoods

items.author: Beveridge & Diamond PC
items.title: Senate Permitting Bill Would Reshape Environmental Permitting And Reviews
items.summary: Law-firm alert, republished on Mondaq because the firm's own site refused scripts. It describes the bill's changes to environmental rules for energy and mineral projects.

quote.text: The bill would dramatically change environmental rules governing project development, especially for energy and mineral projects, by increasing permitting certainty, streamlining permitting processes, limiting litigation
quote.speaker: Beveridge & Diamond

items.author: Josh Freed
items.title: Statement from Climate and Energy SVP Josh Freed on Environmental Group Opposition to Bipartisan Permitting Deal
items.summary: Third Way's climate and energy senior vice president answers the environmental groups' opposition, saying the bill helps transmission and clean energy expansion.

quote.text: This opposition ignores the fact that the bill will be overwhelmingly beneficial to transmission and clean energy expansion in the United States.
quote.speaker: Josh Freed, Third Way

items.outlet: Common Dreams (reprinting a Center for Biological Diversity and Friends of the Earth release)
items.author: Center for Biological Diversity; Friends of the Earth
items.title: Hundreds of Organizations Oppose Endangered Species Attacks in Permitting Legislation
items.summary: More than 200 conservation groups sent Congress a letter urging it to oppose the bill over its Endangered Species Act provisions. The Center for Biological Diversity and Friends of the Earth issued the release.

quote.text: The bill includes sweeping attacks on the Endangered Species Act that would gut protections for nearly every endangered species across the country.
quote.speaker: Center for Biological Diversity and Friends of the Earth (joint release)

letter.ask: Oppose the bill over its Endangered Species Act provisions.

items.outlet: U.S. Senate Committee on Environment and Public Works (majority)
items.author: EPW Majority
items.title: What They're Saying: Bipartisan Permitting Reform Will Deliver Cheaper Energy, More Jobs, Responsible Growth
items.summary: Committee roundup of statements backing the bill from unions, business groups, energy companies, nonprofits, the National Governors Association, the National Association of Counties and a governors' statement.

quote.text: The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act delivers cheaper energy, more well-paying jobs, and responsible growth by accelerating the permitting and construction of critical energy and infrastructure projects while maintaining key environmental and historic preservation safeguards.
quote.speaker: EPW majority press office

items.author: Matthew Zeitlin
items.title: The Crucial Hardhat Union That Has Yet to Endorse the Permitting Bill
items.summary: Heatmap reports that much of the building trades sector is signing on as supporters while the IBEW has not endorsed the bill and says it is still reviewing the language.

quote.text: reviewing the language and holding discussions with stakeholders across our industries.
quote.speaker: IBEW spokesperson

items.author: Joshua Siegel (@SiegelScribe)
items.title: E&C Chair Brett Guthrie says at Punchbowl Tech Summit he wants changes to the grid section
items.summary: Punchbowl reporter Joshua Siegel posts that House Energy and Commerce Chair Brett Guthrie would like changes to the Senate bill's grid section.

quote.text: E&C Chair Brett Guthrie says at @PunchbowlNews Tech Summit that "we absolutely would love to see changes to the" grid section of the Senate's bipartisan permitting bill.
quote.speaker: Joshua Siegel, Punchbowl News (quoting Rep. Brett Guthrie)

items.title: Senate Bipartisan Permitting Reform Package: What Economic Developers Need to Know
items.summary: IEDC explains the 417-page bill for economic developers and describes it as the result of months of bipartisan negotiation.

quote.text: The 417-page bill is the result of months of bipartisan negotiations and would make changes to federal permitting and environmental review processes for energy, infrastructure, and other major projects.
quote.speaker: IEDC

items.author: Robinson Meyer
items.title: Permitting Reform's Battle Lines Are Taking Shape
items.summary: Heatmap Daily reports that, a week after the bill's release, many environmental and climate nonprofits are split on it.

items.author: Sen. Martin Heinrich
items.title: Data center owners should pay for their electricity and any grid upgrades
items.summary: Sen. Martin Heinrich says the bill makes it mandatory for data center owners to pay for their electricity and any grid upgrades.

quote.text: Data center owners should pay for their electricity and any grid upgrades–not you. Our new permitting reform bill makes that mandatory.
quote.speaker: Sen. Martin Heinrich

items.author: Daily Caller News Foundation
items.title: Senators Want To Make AI Data Centers Pay For The Grid Upgrades Driving Up Your Electric Bill
items.summary: The report, citing the AP, says Sen. Mike Lee is confident the Senate will pass the bill in a lame-duck session in November.

quote.text: Lee said he is confident the Senate will pass it in a lame-duck session in November
quote.speaker: Daily Caller News Foundation, citing the AP

items.title: Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026: Permitting Reform County Advocacy Hub
items.summary: NACo's advocacy hub summarizes the bill's county provisions, including cooperating-agency status for counties in NEPA reviews, and gives counties a template letter urging senators to support it.

quote.text: Contact your senators and urge them to support the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026
quote.speaker: National Association of Counties (advocacy hub)

items.author: Axios Future of Energy
items.title: How the permitting bill could collapse
items.summary: Axios lays out how the bill could fail in a lame-duck session and notes that the few definitive statements from lawmakers in both parties are supportive.

quote.text: The few definitive statements on the bill from lawmakers in both parties are supportive.
quote.speaker: Axios

items.author: Greenberg Traurig LLP
items.title: Senate Negotiators Reach Agreement on Permitting Reform Text
items.summary: Law-firm alert summarizing the September 30 text, its mandatory agency deadlines and its streamlined permitting for energy, transmission, pipeline and mining projects.

quote.text: The bill seeks to accelerate energy infrastructure, renewable energy, transmission, pipeline, and mining project approvals through mandatory agency deadlines and streamlined permitting
quote.speaker: Greenberg Traurig

items.outlet: Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources (Democrats)
items.author: Office of Sen. Martin Heinrich
items.title: What They're Saying: Heinrich's Bipartisan Permitting Reform Deal Will Deliver Cheaper Energy, More Jobs, Responsible Growth
items.summary: Heinrich's committee office republishes the supporter roundup and describes the bill's data-center cost provision.

quote.text: ensure that rapidly growing data centers pay the full cost of their associated transmission needs
quote.speaker: Office of Sen. Martin Heinrich (press release)

items.title: What they are saying: manufacturing associations rally behind the bipartisan permitting bill
items.summary: NAM collects statements of support from members of its Council of Manufacturing Associations.

quote.text: The commonsense provisions included in the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act represent an important step forward toward comprehensive permitting reform.
quote.speaker: Ian Jefferies, Association of American Railroads

items.author: David Roberts
items.title: What's up with the new federal permitting reform bill?
items.summary: David Roberts interviews Daniel Palken of Arnold Ventures about the bill's transmission, data-center cost, NEPA and permit-certainty provisions.

quote.text: It brings us to kind of what is the energy sector for? What are we trying to do in this country?
quote.speaker: Daniel Palken, Arnold Ventures

items.author: Brad McElhinny
items.title: Capito says permitting bill would blast away delays and protect approved projects
items.summary: Capito tells MetroNews the White House has made concessions on wind and solar projects and that she was promised the first vote when senators return on November 8.

quote.text: The White House has been right here with us, has made some tremendous concessions
quote.speaker: Sen. Shelley Moore Capito

items.author: Jael Holzman
items.title: Jared Huffman Wants to See Some Changes to the Senate's Permitting Bill
items.summary: Rep. Jared Huffman tells Heatmap that no one will vote on the bill until after the election and says its judgment-fund provision could pay developers without approving their projects.

items.title: Is Trump Trying to Blow Up the Permitting Deal?

quote.speaker: Sen. Roger Wicker

items.title: 185 Groups Slam Permitting Bill's Sweetheart Deal for Data Centers

quote.speaker: American Petroleum Institute (@APIenergy)

items.title: An Unexpected Beneficiary of the Permitting Bill: Mini Marine Power

items.title: U.S. historic preservation law faces the most serious threat in its 60-year history

quote.speaker: Greg Werkheiser, Cultural Heritage Partners

quote.speaker: Josh Freed, Third Way

items.author: Josh Freed

items.title: Post on the no adverse effect clause
items.summary: A group fighting changes to the East Potomac golf course argues the bill's no adverse effect language would let agencies avoid review of harm to historic places with no recourse.

quote.text: It means the executive can shred public lands just by claiming nothing harmful is happening.
quote.speaker: Save East Po

items.author: Save East Po

items.title: NATHPO joins the preservation coalition letter
items.summary: The National Association of Tribal Historic Preservation Officers says it joined preservation groups in a letter objecting to the bill's historic preservation provisions.

quote.text: to express profound objections to numerous provisions impacting historic preservation
quote.speaker: National Association of Tribal Historic Preservation Officers

items.author: NATHPO

items.title: Reply to a Friends of the Earth video
items.summary: Venkatakrishnan calls the claim that the bill could allow a coal plant in the Grand Canyon specious.

quote.text: This is a completely specious, astroturfed attack.
quote.speaker: Pavan Venkatakrishnan, Searchlight Institute

items.author: Pavan Venkatakrishnan
David Jordan
items.title: Permitting bill writers seek industry aid ahead of Senate vote
items.summary: Top aides to the four lead senators told an ACORE conference that the bill is a compromise and asked developers to speak up before the Nov. 9 cloture vote. Roll Call also reports Democratic concern over offshore wind filings and House GOP skepticism.

quote.text: Capital will come off the sidelines because you know your permits are going to be valid no matter what the political lens might happen to be at a given time
quote.speaker: Adam Tomlinson, staff director for Sen. Capito

items.author: Diana DiGangi
items.title: DOJ moves to revoke offshore wind permits, potentially threatening Senate permitting bill
items.summary: Reports that the Justice Department asked federal courts to send back Interior's approvals of the Maryland Offshore Wind, New England Wind and Revolution Wind plans, and that Sen. Whitehouse said the move could blow up the permitting deal.

quote.text: This is how you blow up a permitting deal.
quote.speaker: Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse, D-R.I.

items.outlet: Foley Hoag LLP, Energy & Climate Counsel
items.author: Noah C. Shaw, Kevin Y. Chen
items.title: BAAJA Blast: A Second Wind? Certainty, Cables, and Cost Allocation for Offshore Wind Under the Senate Permitting Bill
items.summary: A law-firm analysis of how the permit-certainty section would bar revocation of offshore wind approvals issued on or after Sept. 16, 2026, with Judgment Fund remedies, and how the transmission sections would affect offshore cables.

quote.text: if enacted, it would make federal approvals far harder to revoke and back that protection with meaningful monetary remedies
quote.speaker: Noah C. Shaw and Kevin Y. Chen, Foley Hoag

items.title: Senate Bill Offers Data Centers A Faster Path To Power, But At A Price
items.summary: Developers quoted by Bisnow disagree on whether the bill helps them. One says faster permits speed the AI buildout; another says the cost rules for loads of 20 MW and more add upfront capital that favors large firms.

quote.text: Upfront capex, especially speculative, is a death knell
quote.speaker: Harmol Samra, CEO, Host Digital

items.outlet: National Trust for Historic Preservation (coalition letter)
items.author: 13 national preservation organizations
items.title: Preservation coalition letter on S. 5653 to Sens. Lee, Capito, Heinrich and Whitehouse
items.summary: Thirteen national preservation groups, including NATHPO and NCSHPO, object to the bill's Section 106 provisions, saying they narrow what is reviewed, set 30-day consultation clocks, let the Interior Secretary take over a THPO's functions and limit judicial review. They ask for substantial revision or removal and propose revisiting the issue next session.

quote.text: achieving that goal requires substantial revisions or removal of the bill's historic preservation provisions
quote.speaker: Preservation coalition letter signers

letter.to: Sens. Mike Lee, Shelley Moore Capito, Martin Heinrich and Sheldon Whitehouse
signers_sample: National Association of Tribal Historic Preservation Officers
National Conference of State Historic Preservation Officers
letter.ask: Substantially revise or remove the bill's historic preservation provisions and take up Section 106 reform next session with the preservation community and Tribal Nations.

items.title: Preservation Coalition Letter on the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act
items.summary: The National Trust posts the coalition letter and says it supports faster reviews but not at the cost of Section 106 protections. It urges senators to oppose the bill as written.

quote.text: We support making federal reviews more efficient and predictable, but not at the expense of these essential protections or the voices of the communities they serve.
quote.speaker: National Trust for Historic Preservation

items.author: Liz Zepeda, Federal Regulatory Director
items.title: "Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act" would roll back environmental protections for communities
items.summary: SELC calls the bill a weakening of environmental review, public notice and the right to challenge permits, and says assurances on wind and solar should be treated with skepticism.

quote.text: Any attempt to speed up permitting will become another tool for the Trump administration to rush construction of polluting energy projects like gas power plants and pipelines.
quote.speaker: Liz Zepeda, Federal Regulatory Director, SELC

items.outlet: Letter hosted by Institute for Progress
items.author: 19 former economic policy and national security officials
items.title: Economic policy and national security leaders support permitting reform
items.summary: Nineteen former officials who served six presidents ask Congress to pass the bill and send it to President Trump, citing competition with China and slow interconnection of new power plants.

quote.text: we believe Congress has a generational opportunity to strengthen our nation's industrial capacity in the face of unprecedented competition from China
quote.speaker: Letter signers

letter.to: Sen. Thune, Sen. Schumer, Speaker Johnson, Rep. Jeffries
letter.ask: Pass the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 and send it to the President.

items.author: Alexander C. Kaufman
items.title: Trump Reopens the Fight Over Orsted's Revolution Wind
items.summary: Briefing on the Justice Department's motion to rescind Interior's approval of Revolution Wind, with the White House response and a joint Whitehouse-Heinrich statement asking for good-faith progress on wind permits.

quote.text: the administration needs to start showing good faith progress on wind permits.
quote.speaker: Sens. Sheldon Whitehouse and Martin Heinrich, joint statement

items.author: Jael Holzman
items.title: The Trump administration is still messing with offshore wind farms
items.summary: Holzman reviews the court filings and asks whether the bill's ban on revoking permits would stop remand motions like these, concluding that the answer depends on how the court-order exception is read once the language is enacted and litigated.

quote.text: Would the court order exception apply to rulings that grant these motions? Or would the developers be able to sue for damages?
quote.speaker: Jael Holzman, Heatmap

items.author: Jael Holzman
items.title: What would happen to Project Jupiter if the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act is passed?
items.summary: Uses a New Mexico gas-powered data center as a test case. Finds the bill would not change Clean Air Act permitting, could lower legal risk for interstate gas pipelines, and would require data centers to pay grid costs.

quote.text: Nothing in the bill would affect requirements that the project adhere to national air emissions standards
quote.speaker: Jael Holzman, Heatmap

items.author: Jael Holzman
items.title: The Data Center Backlash Is Coming for Permitting Reform
items.summary: Reports that LCV, NRDC, Wilderness Society and Earthjustice are pressing the data center fight as the bill nears a vote, and weighs the case that the bill speeds gas-fired data centers through federal land and pipeline permits.

quote.text: In any permutation, this bill is a good thing for data centers
quote.speaker: Brett Hartl, government affairs director, Center for Biological Diversity

items.author: Aidan Mackenzie
items.title: How the Permitting Deal Works
items.summary: A section-by-section explainer by a think tank that supports the bill. It describes the Section 106 rewrite, the data center cost rules in 2107, and the interconnection queue provisions in 2110 and 2111.

quote.text: Section 2301 comprehensively reforms NHPA § 106, codifying much of ACHP's existing regulatory process to protect consultation rights while also streamlining review
quote.speaker: Aidan Mackenzie, Institute for Progress

items.title: Utility lobbying against BAAJA transmission reforms revealed
items.summary: Reports that Oklahoma Gas & Electric is using a lobbying document with Senate offices to seek changes to the transmission sections, including FERC backstop siting, state referral of local planning to FERC and required advanced transmission technology.

quote.text: Oklahoma Gas & Electric, an investor-owned utility company, is lobbying Congress to make “substantial revisions” to the transmission reform sections of major energy legislation
quote.speaker: Energy and Policy Institute

items.title: The proposed U.S. infrastructure permitting reform bill would be a disaster for communities and for climate action
items.summary: An advocacy group argues the bill would speed gas pipelines and power plants for data centers and that Sections 1401 and 1402 could block a future administration from limiting emissions.

quote.text: The bill would strip communities of critical environmental protections, accelerate a massive expansion of gas infrastructure to power AI data centers, and undermine future climate action.
quote.speaker: Oil Change International

items.title: 6 threats to public lands in the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act
items.summary: The group lists six public lands concerns, including the permit lock-in in Section 1401, NEPA changes, limits on judicial review and payments to companies for missed agency deadlines.

quote.text: The bill provides broad loopholes for actions that would no longer be subject to NEPA and eliminates meaningful judicial review
quote.speaker: The Wilderness Society

items.title: Guide to the Impacts of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026
items.summary: A legal analysis that praises the transmission and clean energy provisions and criticizes the permit certainty sections and limits on judicial review. The page shows no publication date; the item date is the date the page was read.

quote.text: The permit certainty provisions would also exacerbate current erosion of the rule of law.
quote.speaker: Earthjustice

items.title: DOJ moves to kill offshore wind permits as Congress weighs permitting bill
items.summary: A daily newsletter item reports that DOJ asked judges to revoke approvals for three offshore wind farms, and that more than 100 groups wrote Congress on Oct. 22 urging rejection of the bill over public lands.

quote.text: More than 100 groups urged Congress in a letter Thursday to reject the Senate permitting bill from Senators Whitehouse, Heinrich, Capito and Lee due to its negative impacts on public lands.
quote.speaker: Center for Western Priorities

items.title: What the Senate’s Permitting Bill Could Mean for Hunters and Anglers
items.summary: A sportsmen's conservation group supports permitting certainty but asks Congress to revise Sections 1401 and 1402 so agencies keep the ability to enforce permit conditions and respond to new information about fish and wildlife.

quote.text: TRCP supports efforts to provide greater permitting certainty and is actively encouraging Congress to revise Sections 1401 and 1402
quote.speaker: Theodore Roosevelt Conservation Partnership

items.author: API and 137 organizations
items.title: Broad Coalition of 130+ Groups Urge Congress to Pass Bipartisan Permitting Reform This Year
items.summary: API and 137 organizations from energy, labor, manufacturing, housing and transportation ask House and Senate leaders to bring S. 5653 to the floor and pass it before the end of the year.

quote.text: permitting reform presents Congress with one of its most consequential opportunities to address affordability this Congress
quote.speaker: Coalition letter signers, as quoted by API

letter.ask: Bring S. 5653 to the floor and pass it before the end of the year.

items.author: Julia Conley
items.title: Analysis Warns Bipartisan Senate Permitting Bill Would Lock In Trump-Era Data Center, Fossil Fuel Approvals
items.summary: Reports an analysis by the Center for Western Priorities' Aaron Weiss on Sections 1401 and 1402, with comment from law professor Justin Pidot on court-ordered environmental reviews.

quote.text: A judge can send the review back for a redo, but construction continues in the meantime, and Section 1401 bars the agency from changing the permit based on what the new review finds
quote.speaker: Aaron Weiss, Center for Western Priorities

items.outlet: Signatory Wall and Ceiling Contractors Alliance (report of the letter)
items.title: Nine Democratic State Attorneys General Raise Concerns Over Bipartisan Permitting Reform Bill
items.summary: A trade alliance reports that nine Democratic attorneys general, led by California, Massachusetts and Washington, wrote Senate leaders and the EPW and ENR committees, backing the bill's goals while objecting to provisions on state authority. The letter text was not found, so this is a secondhand report.

quote.text: the attorneys general warned that certain provisions would undermine state authority under the Clean Water Act and National Historic Preservation Act
quote.speaker: SWACCA summary of the AG letter

letter.to: Senate leadership and the Senate Environment and Public Works and Energy and Natural Resources Committees
letter.ask: A meeting with congressional leaders to discuss changes to the bill.

items.author: People's Environmental Justice Caucus
items.title: People’s Environmental Justice Caucus opposes Senate permitting reform bill
items.summary: The House caucus founded by Reps. Tlaib, Lee and Grijalva opposes the bill, citing data center and gas pipeline construction, limits on court challenges and risks to Tribal sacred sites.

quote.text: The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 is a gift to Big Oil and Big Tech.
quote.speaker: People's Environmental Justice Caucus

items.author: Editorial board
items.title: On confirmations, permitting and a senator who has some explanations to make
items.summary: An editorial agrees permitting needs reform but says Sen. Heinrich will have to explain to environmental and Tribal allies why he co-sponsored a bill that changes the National Historic Preservation Act and other laws.

quote.text: Tribal nations across the United States are uniformly opposed — they believe changes to the National Historic Preservation Act would severely reduce the ability of Native governments to speak up and protect sacred sites.
quote.speaker: The Santa Fe New Mexican editorial board
